question.text: Asha Deep Trust (women empowerment NPO, 12AB registered) earned total income of INR 80 lakh during FY 2024-25 from grants and investment returns. For the income to remain exempt under Section 11, what is the MINIMUM amount the Trust must apply towards its charitable objectives during the year (ignoring corpus and accumulation options)?

answer.text: INR 80,00,000 — 100% of income must be applied each year without exception
INR 60,00,000 — 75% of income must be applied each year
INR 68,00,000 — 85% of income must be applied each year
INR 16,00,000 — 20% of income (aggregate receipts cap for general public utility)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 11 of the Income Tax Act, an NPO must apply at least 85% of its income earned during the year towards its charitable objectives to retain exemption. 85% of INR 80,00,000 = INR 68,00,000. If application falls short, the balance can be accumulated (subject to filing specific forms and investing in specified instruments) for application within a maximum of 5 years. The Trap: 100% is incorrect — the Act permits 15% to be retained for future use without losing exemption. 75% confuses the 85%/15% split with a 75%/25% framework from unrelated tax sections. The 20% figure is the aggregate-receipts cap for incidental business of general public utility objects, not the overall application threshold. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) covers 85% application as part of HNI philanthropy planning. XXIII focuses on how the SIA must reconcile 'applied for objectives' in the ITR with 'programmatic spend' in the Annual Impact Report — the two numbers should agree. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When auditing a NPO under SAS-100, reconcile the 'applied towards objectives' figure in Form 10B Schedule I with the programmatic expenditure you certify in the AIR. A gap of more than 5% should be investigated — often it reflects capital expenditure or accumulations that the SE has not clearly disclosed in its impact narrative.
